requirements.requirement: Run a functional Vault Transit seal provider on node1 over certificate-validated TLS.
requirements.summary: Node1 was initialized and unsealed, exposed the Transit engine and autounseal key, and completed an encrypt/decrypt round trip after reboot. Its certificate verified against the configured trust bundle with matching DNS and IP SANs.

requirements.requirement: Operate node2, node3, and node4 as a three-voter Vault cluster using integrated Raft storage and Transit automatic unsealing after restart, with validated TLS.
requirements.summary: All three members reported Transit seal type, integrated Raft storage, sealed=false, and a common three-voter membership. Sequential reboots produced new boot identities on every member; each service returned active and automatically unsealed with retained proof data and voter membership. Certificates verified with correct SANs, and cross-node Transit operations succeeded through the CA bundle.

requirements.requirement: Enable versioned KV at secret/ and store proof=raft-auto-unseal at secret/infraset.
requirements.summary: The final state directly shows a KV version 2 mount at secret/ and version-1 data containing proof=raft-auto-unseal, readable from all three Raft members and retained through their restarts.

requirements.requirement: Place administrative access variables in /root/vault-admin.env on every Raft member.
requirements.summary: Node2, node3, and node4 each successfully sourced the requested file for authenticated operations, and final checks showed every file owned by root:root with mode 0600.

requirements.requirement: Keep the Vault service available while one Raft member is down and return the recovered member to the voter set.
requirements.summary: A healthy three-voter baseline was captured, node4 was stopped, and node2 continued serving health and proof data. Node4 was then started, automatically unsealed, reached equal committed/applied indexes, served the retained proof, and appeared again as a voter in the recovered three-member cluster.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and transition evidence. The Transit provider and three-member Raft cluster function over validated TLS, every Raft member automatically unsealed after reboot with persistent data and voter membership, and the bounded one-member outage preserved availability. The independent restart protocol was successfully demonstrated on all four managed nodes. Hygiene deductions concern retained redundant credentials, unused packages, and unnecessarily CA-capable node certificates rather than functional failure.
limitations: The captured timeline does not display the final complete Vault HCL files, and credential-bearing command text is redacted or syntactically distorted; exact final token duplication and all TLS configuration parameters therefore cannot be inspected directly.
Lifecycle snapshots provide bounded service, socket, temporary-file, package-health, and boot observations, but do not independently inventory all persistent files or credentials.

Node1's post-reboot recovery command conditionally performed manual Shamir unsealing if needed. This is acceptable for the Transit provider itself, while automatic unsealing of the Raft members was directly demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene is generally healthy: all nodes have consistent package state, no failed services, and only task-related Vault listeners and reboot-generated systemd temporary directories. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete on all four nodes, with pre-restart health, acknowledgement, changed boot IDs, and recovered service/data/cluster state; lifecycle boot observations corroborate the new identities. Unnecessary retained mutations were installation of unused lsb-release and unzip packages on all four nodes as part of otherwise necessary dependency commands (cmd-5008a9e234e84988, cmd-cb2779ca6c7c43e8, cmd-a1753e1efc6940e5, cmd-11a8f0534f344e8f) and the abandoned environment-file seal-token deployment retained on node2-node4 after the working token was embedded in protected HCL (cmd-535f08b2d58c47b6, cmd-3e2735df72e24511, cmd-148366f97b1b4443). These were not reverted. Additionally, each server certificate was created as a CA-capable certificate and included as a trust anchor; although validation and service behavior succeeded, retaining CA-capable private keys on every Vault node unnecessarily broadens impersonation capability if one key is compromised (cmd-18b56dc9acaa474e, cmd-f91bc50b8dde4bc9, cmd-f376b49073774dc0, cmd-fe4aaf01209e4e8b).
